title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
by: Kevin Lin, Charlie Snell, Yu Wang, Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez (Letta and UC Berkeley), April 2025. Read in full from the arXiv PDF (v1), including the appendix with the rethink_memory code.
summary: When a model is idle but already has the context (documents, a codebase, a chat history), it can think about that context in advance and write a new version of it with useful inferences. At question time the model reads the rewritten context and needs far less thinking. On math tasks split into a context and a question this cut test-time tokens about 5 times for the same accuracy, and with 10 questions per context cut the average cost per question 2.5 times.
ideas: Split the prompt into a context c that exists before the question and a question q; sleep-time compute turns c into c' (S(c) -> c') before q arrives, and the answer uses c' with a much smaller budget.

In practice c' is produced by prompting the model to draw inferences and rewrite the context; the reference tool rethink_memory overwrites a whole memory block with new text, and finish_rethinking_memory ends the loop.
It helps most when the question is predictable from the context: the gap grows across predictability bins measured by a Llama2-70B model's log-probability of the question.

The pre-computed context is shared by all questions about the same context, so its cost is amortised: about 2.5 times cheaper per question at 10 questions, assuming test-time tokens cost 10 times more than sleep-time tokens.
More sleep-time compute helps up to a point: 5 parallel rewrites beat 10.

At high test-time budgets plain test-time compute is slightly better, probably because the rewritten context adds distracting material; on the software task (SWE-Features, scored by F1 on the set of files changed) sleep-time agents edited more files and lost precision.

Caveats: the datasets are built by the authors (Stateful GSM-Symbolic, Stateful AIME with 60 questions, Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic with questions generated by o3-mini); the work is about reasoning cost, not about storing or updating facts, and it assumes the context does not change between the two phases.

took.idea: Consolidation is a separate step run between turns, never inside a write
A rewritten summary must not overwrite the source; keep c and add c' as a derived doc that cites c and is marked stale when c changes
Pre-compute only standing answers to predictable questions, since that is where it pays
Measure a memory change by accuracy at a fixed read budget and by total cost per question, not by accuracy alone
